title: Operating Systems
subject: core-cs
description: Core principles of operating system design: process and thread management, CPU scheduling, synchronization, deadlocks, and memory management with virtual memory. Each unit pairs lecture notes with fully worked numerical examples of the kind set in examinations.

units.title: Unit 1 · Processes and CPU Scheduling
units.description: The process abstraction, threads, interprocess communication and CPU scheduling algorithms.

topics.title: Processes and Threads
topics.description: Process states, the PCB, context switching, fork and exec, threading models and IPC mechanisms.

documents.title: Processes and Threads — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Process states, PCB contents, a fork/exec example in C, user versus kernel threads, multithreading models, and pipes, shared memory and message passing.

topics.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms
topics.description: Scheduling criteria, FCFS, SJF, SRTF, priority, round robin and multilevel feedback queues.

documents.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Scheduling criteria, each major algorithm with its trade-offs, the convoy effect, starvation and aging, and multilevel feedback queues.

documents.title: CPU Scheduling — Worked Gantt-Chart Example
documents.description: Gantt charts with waiting, turnaround and response times for FCFS, SJF, SRTF and Round Robin on one four-process workload.

units.title: Unit 2 · Synchronization and Deadlocks
units.description: Coordinating concurrent processes safely and preventing, avoiding or detecting deadlock.

topics.title: Process Synchronization
topics.description: Race conditions, the critical-section problem, Peterson's solution, mutexes, semaphores, monitors and classic problems.

documents.title: Process Synchronization — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Race conditions, the three critical-section requirements, Peterson's algorithm, hardware primitives, mutexes, semaphores and monitors.

documents.title: Classic Synchronization Problems — Study Guide
documents.description: Semaphore solutions and pitfalls for the bounded-buffer, readers-writers and dining-philosophers problems.

topics.title: Deadlocks
topics.description: Coffman conditions, resource-allocation graphs, prevention, avoidance, detection and recovery.

documents.title: Deadlocks — Lecture Notes
documents.description: The four necessary conditions, resource-allocation graphs, safe states, and prevention versus avoidance versus detection.

documents.title: Banker's Algorithm — Fully Worked Example
documents.description: Need matrix, a step-by-step safe-sequence derivation, and three resource requests that are granted, delayed and denied.

units.title: Unit 3 · Memory and Storage Management
units.description: Physical and virtual memory management, and file systems.

topics.title: Memory Management and Virtual Memory
topics.description: Contiguous allocation, fragmentation, paging, TLBs, segmentation, demand paging, page replacement and thrashing.

documents.title: Memory Management: Allocation, Paging and Segmentation — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Fit strategies, fragmentation, address translation, page-table sizing, TLB effective access time and segmentation.

documents.title: Virtual Memory and Page Replacement — Worked Examples
documents.description: Demand paging and page-fault cost, FIFO, Optimal and LRU traces on one reference string, Belady's anomaly, and the working-set model.

topics.title: File Systems
topics.description: Materials for this topic will be published later in the term.
